chapters.title: The three local areas: working directory, staging area, repository
CI/CD, AI and the daily route

takeaways: Git is a local-first version control system that records deliberate, named checkpoints called commits, so you can see what changed and return to an earlier version.
Changes move from the working directory through the staging area into the local repository, while branches let you work safely without disturbing the trusted main version.
GitHub adds a shared remote repository and pull requests for review and automated checks, turning separate computers into one team workflow: work, stage, commit, push, review, merge.
hook: If your project folders are named final, final-final and use-this-one, Git is the fix. This episode explains Git in plain English for beginners, makers and Microsoft 365 builders: commits, the staging area, branches, merges, conflicts and how GitHub and pull requests fit into a team workflow.
